He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2021 class. ==High school career== Christie played basketball for [[Rolling Meadows High School]] in [[Rolling Meadows, Illinois]], and was teammates with his younger brother, [[Cam Christie|Cameron]].{{cite web |last=Narang |first=Bob |title=For Rolling Meadows phenom Max Christie, life in the spotlight is the new normal |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/arlington-heights/sports/ct-ahp-boys-basketball-max-christie-rolling-meadows-tl-1219-20191214-wjwd2xcv35fhdoyh5pc76ir6j4-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=June 20, 2021 |date=December 13, 2019}} In his freshman season, he averaged 20 points, nine rebounds and four assists per game.{{cite web |last=Narang |first=Bob |title=Must-see Mustang: Max Christie a game-changer at Rolling Meadows |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/arlington-heights/sports/ct-ahp-boys-basketball-rolling-meadows-max-christie-tl-1115-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=June 20, 2021 |date=November 10, 2018}} As a sophomore, Christie averaged 25.5 points, 10 rebounds and 3.2 assists per game. He scored a career-high 51 points against [[Elk Grove High School (Elk Grove Village, Illinois)|Elk Grove High School]].{{cite web |last=Quinn |first=Brendan |date=July 7, 2020 |title=Max Christie picks Michigan State as Tom Izzo's recruiting haul continues |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1914378/2020/07/07/max-christie-picks-michigan-state-as-tom-izzos-recruiting-haul-continues/ |access-date=June 20, 2021 |website=[[The Athletic]] |via=The New York Times}} In his junior season, Christie averaged 25 points and 11 rebounds per game, earning [[Pioneer Press]] Player of the Year honors.{{cite web |last=Reaven |first=Steve |title=Rolling Meadows' Max Christie is the 2019–20 Pioneer Press Boys Basketball Player of the Year |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/arlington-heights/sports/ct-ahp-boys-basketball-pioneer-poy-max-christie-tl-0326-20200321-5gdotc3ncbbdhl7ketqi7e4zyu-story.html |website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |access-date=June 20, 2021 |date=March 21, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 24 points, 10.1 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 3.1 steals per game, leading his team to a 15–0 record. Christie was selected as ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' Player of the Year, ''[[The News-Gazette (Champaign–Urbana)|News-Gazette]]'' All-State Player of the Year and Illinois [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last=Richey |first=Scott |title=N-G All-State POY: Christie cemented legacy at Rolling Meadows ===Los Angeles Lakers / South Bay Lakers (2022–2025)=== ===2022–23=== Christie was selected by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in the second round of the [[2022 NBA draft]] with the 35th overall pick. Christie joined the Lakers' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612747/lakers |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} In his Summer League debut, Christie scored five points and nine rebounds in a 100–66 California Classic win against the [[Miami Heat]].{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers vs Miami Heat Jul 2, 2022 Box Scores |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lal-vs-mia-1322200001/box-score#box-score |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} On July 8, 2022, Christie signed his rookie scale contract with the Lakers.{{Cite web |date=July 8, 2022 |title=Lakers Sign Max Christie |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-sign-max-christie-070722 |access-date=July 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} During his rookie season, he scored a season-high 14 points on 6 of 8 shooting and 2-of-3 made [[Three-point field goal]]s on January 10 in a 122–109 loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web |title=Nuggets 122–109 Lakers (10 Jan, 2023) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401468764 |website=ESPN UK |access-date=November 16, 2025}} He was assigned to the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the [[NBA G League]] on March 8, 2023.{{Cite web |last=Siegel |first=Brett |date=March 8, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Make A Roster Move Following Win Over Grizzlies On Tuesday Night |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/los-angeles-lakers-assign-max-christie-to-south-bay-lakers-nba-g-league-03-08-23 |access-date=August 13, 2025 |website=SI.com}} He was recalled by the Los Angeles Lakers from South Bay two days later.{{Cite web |last=Siegel |first=Brett |date=March 10, 2023 |title=Los Angeles Lakers Make A Roster Move Ahead Of Friday Night Game Against Raptors |url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/news/los-angeles-lakers-recall-max-christie-south-bay-lakers-nba-g-league-3-10-23 |access-date=August 13, 2025 |website=SI.com}} For the season, he averaged 3.1 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 1 assist a game on 41.5% [[Field goal (basketball)|2s]] and 41.9% shooting on 1.5 [[Three-point field goal|threes]] per game.{{cite news |title=Max Christie Career Stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4432582/max-christie |access-date=November 16, 2025 |publisher=ESPN |date=November 16, 2025}} During the [[2023 NBA playoffs|playoffs]], in 3.7 minutes per game, he scored 1.4 points per game on 25% shooting from the three-point line and 50% shooting from [[Field goal (basketball)|two]].{{cite web |title=Max Christie – Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and More |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chrisma02.html |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=November 16, 2025}} ===2023–24=== On December 9, 2023, Christie and the Lakers won the [[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament|inaugural season]] of the [[NBA In-Season Tournament]].{{Cite web |last=Bontemps |first=Tim |date=December 10, 2023 |title=Lakers win in-season tournament final behind Anthony Davis' 41–20 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39080368 |access-date=December 10, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} Max tied his career high with 14 points twice during the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]], first against the [[Miami Heat]] during a 110–96 loss on January 3,{{cite web |title=Heat 110–96 Lakers (Jan 4, 2024) |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401585103 |website=ESPN |access-date=December 16, 2025}} and secondly against the [[Phoenix Suns]] eight days later during a 127–109 loss.{{cite web |title=Suns 127–109 Lakers (Jan 12, 2024) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401585159 |website=ESPN |access-date=December 16, 2025}} For the season, his minutes went up to 14.1 from the previous season but his three-point percentage dipped on slightly more attempts while most of his numbers remained steady. ===2024–25=== Christie re-signed with the Lakers on a four-year, $32 million deal on July 2, 2024.{{cite web |date=June 30, 2024 |title=Sources: Max Christie to stay with Lakers on 4-year, $32M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40468897 |access-date=July 4, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}{{cite web |author=Wong |first=S. |date=July 6, 2024 |title=Lakers Re-Sign Max Christie |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-re-sign-max-christie-070624 |access-date=July 14, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} When the Lakers hired head coach [[JJ Redick]] in the summer of 2024, the two got together to work out in Las Vegas ahead of the start of the [[2024–25 NBA season|2024–25 season]].{{cite web |last1=Rude |first1=Jacob |title=Lakers: Max Christie worked out with JJ Redick during Summer League |url=https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2024/7/29/24209282/max-christie-lakers-jj-redick-las-vegas-workout-offseason-summer-league |website=Silver Screen & Roll |access-date=November 16, 2025}} When the season started, he shot only 25% in October and 31% in November on three-point shots.{{cite web |last1=Ogden |first1=Maxwell |title=Lakers confirm Max Christie has locked in an essential role in the rotation |url=https://lakeshowlife.com/lakers-confirm-max-christie-locked-essential-role-rotation |website=Lake Show Life |access-date=November 16, 2025}} However, after becoming a starter, he shot over 45% on threes over the next eight games while averaging 10.6 point a game over that stretch.{{cite web |title=2024–25 Los Angeles Lakers Schedule |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/LAL/2025_games.html |website=Basketball-Reference |access-date=November 16, 2025}} Over the subsequent 17 games, he continued to shoot the three-point shot well, making nearly 41% from the three-point line and averaging 10.9 points per game. Overall for the Lakers in the 2024–25 season, Christie shot 37% on three-pointers during 25 minutes a game – nearly double that of the previous season, while averaging 8.5 points per game. Throughout the season, he earned high praise for his defense from Lakers' stars such as [[LeBron James]]{{cite news |last1=Woike |first1=Dan |title=With Anthony Davis Out, LeBron James and Max Christie lead Lakers past Portland |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/lakers/story/2025-01-02/lebron-james-max-christie-lakers-portland-trail-blazers |access-date=November 16, 2025 |publisher=Los Angeles Times |date=January 2, 2025}}{{cite news |last1=Spears |first1=Marc |title=Dallas Mavericks guard Max Christie Prepared for opportunity after trade from Lakers |url=https://andscape.com/features/dallas-mavericks-guard-max-christie-prepared-for-opportunity-after-trade-from-lakers/ |access-date=November 16, 2025 |publisher=Andscape |date=February 6, 2025}} [[Anthony Davis]],{{cite web |title=Spectrum Sportsnet on X: Anthony Davis discusses the Lakers performance on defense and down the stretch and the final minute of the game |url=https://x.com/SpectrumSN/status/1863443880017809523 |website=X.com |access-date=November 16, 2025}} [[Austin Reaves]],{{cite web | last=Garcia | first=Edwin | title=Austin Reaves praises Max Christie for 'phenomenal' defense against Ja Morant | website=Silver Screen and Roll|publisher=SB Nation | date=December 16, 2024 | url=https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2024/12/16/24322605/lakers-austin-reaves-max-christie-defense-ja-morant-grizzlies | access-date=December 10, 2025}} as well as coach Redick. During the first 2 1/2 months of the season, he increased his career-high in points for a game three times, with 15 on December 13 against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]],{{cite web |title=Timberwolves 97–87 Lakers (December 14, 2024) |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401736804 |website=ESPN |access-date=November 16, 2025}} 17 against the [[Detroit Pistons]] 10 days later,{{cite web |title=Pistons 117–114 Lakers (December 24, 2024) Box Score |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401704970 |website=ESPN |access-date=November 16, 2024}} and then with 28 against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] on January 2, 2025.{{cite web |title=Lakers 114–106 Trail Blazers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401705034 |website=ESPN |access-date=November 16, 2025}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2025–present)=== ===2024–25 season=== {{See also|Luka Dončić–Anthony Davis trade}} On February 2, 2025, Christie was traded alongside [[Anthony Davis]] and a 2029 first-round pick to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Luka Dončić]], [[Maxi Kleber]] and [[Markieff Morris]]. The Mavericks additionally traded a 2025 second-round pick to the [[Utah Jazz]], who also acquired [[Jalen Hood-Schifino]] and a 2025 second-round pick from the Lakers.{{cite web|first=Eddie|last=Sefko|title=Mavericks acquire Anthony Davis for Luka Dončić|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-get-ad/|website=Mavs.com|date=February 2, 2025|access-date=February 2, 2025}} Over the remainder of the 2024–25 season he increased his scoring to 11.2 points per game while shooting 36.4% on threes and playing 30 minutes a game. His highest scoring game for the Mavericks in 2025 was 23.{{cite web |title=Mavericks 116–105 Rockets (February 8, 2025) |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game/_/gameId/401705307/rockets-mavericks |website=ESPN |access-date=November 16, 2025}} ===2025–26 season=== Christie averaged 12.8 points a game over the first 20 games of the season while shooting 47% from three-point shots and playing in every game.{{cite web |title=Max Christie 2025–26 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chrisma02/gamelog/2026 |website=Basketball Reference |access-date=February 1, 2026}} Between January 18 and 25, Christie had four straight 20 point scoring games, including a game against the [[New York Knicks]] in which he made a career-high eight three-pointers.{{cite news |last1=Afseth |first1=Grant |title=NBA News: Max Christie's Eight-Three Night At Madison Square Garden Signals Elite Potential for Dallas Mavericks |url=https://dallashoopsjournal.com/p/max-christie-eight-threes-madison-square-garden-dallas-mavericks-nba-news/ |access-date=February 1, 2026 |publisher=Dallas Hoops Journal |date=January 20, 2026}} ==National team career== Christie represented the [[United States men's national under-17 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-16 Americas Championship]] in Brazil. He averaged 9.5 points and 3.3 rebounds per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |last=Solari |first=Chris |title=Michigan State basketball adds 'special, unique kid' in 5-star SG Max Christie |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2020/07/07/michigan-state-basketball-max-christie-tom-izzo-2021-recruiting/5394162002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=June 20, 2021 |date=July 7, 2020}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
